title: Reorder List
statement: Reorder the list, given as values, from L0, L1, ..., Ln into L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, L2, ... Find the middle, reverse the second half, and merge the halves by rewiring pointers.
hints: The slow and fast pointers find the start of the second half. Fast moves two steps, slow moves one.
Reverse the second half in place.
Merge by alternating one node from the first half and one node from the reversed second half.

approaches.name: Array of nodes
approaches.explanation: Index the ends toward the middle.

editorial: Split after the middle so the first half is at least as long as the second. Reverse the second half, then weave: each step takes the next first-half node and the next second-half node. The weave ends when the second half is exhausted. A middle node of an odd-length list remains at the end of the first half.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def reorder_list(head: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, value: int, nxt=None):
            self.value = value
            self.nxt = nxt

    if len(head) < 2:
        return head[:]
    dummy = Node(0)
    tail = dummy
    for value in head:
        tail.nxt = Node(value)
        tail = tail.nxt
    slow, fast = dummy.nxt, dummy.nxt
    while fast and fast.nxt:
        slow = slow.nxt
        fast = fast.nxt.nxt
    prev = None
    cur = slow
    while cur:
        nxt = cur.nxt
        cur.nxt = prev
        prev = cur
        cur = nxt
    first = dummy.nxt
    second = prev
    while second.nxt:
        nxt1, nxt2 = first.nxt, second.nxt
        first.nxt = second
        second.nxt = nxt1
        first, second = nxt1, nxt2
    out = []
    node = dummy.nxt
    while node:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.nxt
    return out
